record.paper_title: Open Problems in Geometry and Topology
record.original_question: Is the smooth 4-dimensional Poincaré conjecture true? Equivalently, if X is a compact 4-manifold with vanishing π1(X) and π2(X), must X be diffeomorphic to the 4-sphere S^4?

evidence.quote: Is the smooth, 4-dimensional Poincare conjecture true? That is, if a compact, 4-dimensional manifold has vanishing π1 and π2, is it necessary diffeomorphic to S^4?

artifact.self_contained_problem: Smooth 4-dimensional Poincaré conjecture. Let X be a compact, connected, smooth 4-dimensional manifold (without boundary) such that the fundamental group π_1(X) and the second homotopy group π_2(X) both vanish. Must X be diffeomorphic to the standard 4-sphere S^4? Equivalently, is every smooth 4-manifold that is homotopy equivalent to S^4 diffeomorphic to S^4?
artifact.status_search_result: The smooth 4-dimensional Poincaré conjecture remains one of the central open problems in topology as of 2026. Freedman (1982) settled the topological version, but the smooth case is unresolved. Several recent claimed proofs (e.g., by Akbulut, Etesi, Svancara) exist but have not gained community acceptance.
